newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude firm on spread buying, volume slack.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude firm on spread buying, volume slack.

text.p: NYMEX crude was firm Thursday afternoon on buying in the nearby calendar spread ahead of April crude's expiry at session's end.
"We had some refiner buying in the April/May spread for purely speculative purposes, but most players are on the sidelines," said a New York crude trader.
At 1434 EST, April crude was up 19 cents at $22.23 a barrel with the April/May spread rising to 38 cents from 22 cents Wednesday.
Traders said the strong expiry so far belied a weaker backwardation in the back month spreads, suggesting crude may end the week on shakier ground once May became the spot month.
Gains in refined products trailed crude's, with April gasoline up 0.29 cent a gallon at 68.25 cents and April heating oil up 0.31 cent a gallon at 56.60 cents.
"Gasoline is still being supported by those who think the crack spread will be strong," said a New York gasoline trader.
The April gasoline-to-crude crack spread had weakened 17 cents to $6.33 a barrel from Wednesday, although the level was still historically high.
